Text:
Rowers race toward a finish line they cannot see.

That observation sits at the heart of 776BC’s As One / The Pursuit. It is specific to the sport, and strong enough to carry beyond its first telling.

This case study follows the idea as it moves through a small editorial system: the source story, a pull quote, a long read and selected stills.

The question behind the work: how do you give more people a way into the same story without losing what made it matter?

#776BC #BrandStorytelling

A story can meet people in different moments.

For 776BC’s The Pursuit, the same central idea appears as a pull quote, a longer editorial read and a sequence of selected stills. Each gives the audience a different way in. Each stays close to the source.

The examples here are drawn from the Pursuit page. They show the editorial range of one story, not a claim about reach or performance.

Explore the Pursuit page: https://optiflows.com.au/776bc/pursuit/

#776BC #ContentSystems

The useful part of a content system is the sequence of decisions.

Start with a story worth carrying. Draft only the versions that serve a purpose. Check each one for meaning, context and brand. Then decide what is ready to distribute.

That is the operating model this 776BC case study is designed to show. The goal is consistency and human control as the story moves across formats, not a bigger asset count for its own sake.
